audit.whatIsWrong: Cross-layer chart disagreement: content win[2..5] read "Cassiopeia" while full phases[2..5].side read "Skill", and win[6] "Azir" vs phases[6].side "Skill".
audit.why: Packet levelChart and the 48.72% win rate both put Cassiopeia ahead through the first item; Azir's full-build wall against a champion with no dash is the flip.
audit.corrected: Cassiopeia x6 then Azir, both layers, with every changed why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] and mid/late prose called her ultimate "Petrify" and claimed a level-6 range/duration increase and a Twin Fang "execute"; spikes[0] used the fabricated "Noxious Blight" and attributed grounding to it.
audit.why: Her R is Petrifying Gaze (120/100/80, 825 range) and stuns only enemies facing her. Grounding is Miasma (W), 24/22/20/18/16. Twin Fang (0.75s, 700) deals bonus damage to poisoned targets and heals — Riot's text says nothing about an execute.
audit.corrected: Real names and real numbers; level-6 spike framed as the facing-dependent stun into a 0.75s Twin Fang, late spike as Emperor's Divide walling a dashless champion.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit; the decisive interaction (Miasma grounding disables Shifting Sands) was stated without either cooldown.
audit.why: Miasma 24/22/20/18/16 vs Azir E 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 — the two long cooldowns in the lane, and hers turns his off. Noxious Blast is 3.5s and Twin Fang 0.75s, so her chip never stops.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns stated, and the grounding-vs-E interaction made the step-up rule.
sources: brief.ownerKit E flags 'dash: mobility that grounding and walls can deny'

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds timing was not tied to Twin Fang anywhere in the lane text.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal: Twin Fang heals Cassiopeia for a percentage of damage dealt, so extended trades swing on anti-heal.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into breakdown.feeding and breakdown.carry.

audit.why: 48.72% over 234 games matches a TRICKY 7/10 rating.

edits.before: Two soldiers up means a real trade: W-Q the drag-through and step back. The poke is free only when his engage is down.
edits.after: Two soldiers up means a real trade: W-Q the drag-through and step back. The poke is free only when her Miasma is down.

edits.before: E completes the safety net — you now have the shield-dash out. Greedier soldier placements are allowed, not encouraged.
edits.after: Miasma grounds you, so your 22-second E is not an escape while the cloud is down — and her Q returns every 3.5s to chip you.

edits.before: Nashor's components arrive and the soldier DPS starts to sting. Drag Qs through Cassiopeia on every last-hit he takes.
edits.after: Nashor's components sting, but Twin Fang fires every 0.75s and heals her through your chip — she still wins the long trade.

edits.before: Emperor's Divide online — the dive insurance and the insec flip. With R up you win every 2v2 your jungler joins.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns anyone facing her into a Twin Fang follow-up; your R answers only if you spend it as she steps up.

edits.before: Nashor's spike: your soldier poke becomes shred. Shove crashes and rotate — the soldiers siege towers better than any mid.
edits.after: Nashor's makes your poke shred, but her poison clears waves just as fast and Miasma still fences off the ground you need.

edits.before: Full build Azir is a teamfight: R cuts the fight in half, soldiers melt whoever is on your side of the wall.
edits.after: Full build flips it: Cassiopeia has no dash, so Emperor's Divide walls her off her team and the soldiers finish her.

edits.before: Petrify range increase at this stage creates deadly stun-into-burst combos you can't escape
edits.after: Twin Fang fires every 0.75s and heals her, so she wins any trade that lasts past your poke

edits.before: Her scaling advantage compounds further as Twin Fang execute damage grows with levels
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns anyone facing her and hands Twin Fang a free burst window

edits.before: Soldier range vs spell range — poke through the wave he has to stand in, and dodge the answer he throws back.
edits.after: Soldier range beats her 850 Q, but Miasma grounds your escape — poke from outside it and never dash through the cloud.

edits.before: Out-poke through soldiers, dodge the answer, and out-scale into the siege machine he cannot match. Keep one eye on Miasma and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Out-poke through soldiers and refuse the extended trade Twin Fang wins. Miasma is 16-24s: her cloud on cooldown is your only window to step up, dash, or commit.

edits.before: Cassiopeia wins by landing Miasma, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Cassiopeia wins by grounding you in Miasma, poisoning with Noxious Blast, and healing through it all with Twin Fang.

edits.before: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Cassiopeia on his last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — two-second trades he cannot answer without overextending.
edits.after: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Cassiopeia on her last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — short trades she cannot answer without walking into your sand.

edits.before: Standing at max soldier range admiring your poke with E on cooldown — that is the engage window every Cassiopeia player is waiting for.
edits.after: Standing inside Miasma to squeeze one more soldier auto — grounded, slowed and poisoned, you hand Twin Fang the extended trade it wins.

edits.before: Ahead, siege: crash waves with soldier autos, take every plate, and rotate to river with R held — your wall converts even fights into massacres.
edits.after: Ahead, siege: crash with soldier autos, take every plate, and rotate with R held — Cassiopeia has no dash, so a wall behind her ends any fight she starts.

edits.before: - Azir vs Cassiopeia - Track: Cassiopeia Miasma. - Poke through soldiers on his last-hits — never step past your own sand. - No commits into Miasma. - The ultimate closes arguments; it doesn’t open them.
edits.after: - Azir vs Cassiopeia - Track: Miasma, 16-24s. - Poke through soldiers on her last-hits — never step past your own sand. - Grounded means no E: no commits into the cloud. - R walls her; she has no dash.

edits.before: - Cassiopeia Miasma: matchup-defining — Grounds you — dashes and leaps are disabled inside it. Check it before every step-up. - E Shifting Sands is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Miasma is 24s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5, and it grounds — your E will not fire inside it. Check the cloud before every step-up. - Noxious Blast is 3.5s so the chip never stops; Twin Fang every 0.75s. - Petrifying Gaze 120/100/80.

edits.before: If Cassiopeia gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Miasma extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm at soldier range and stay relevant through wave control.
edits.after: If Cassiopeia gets a kill, give Miasma extra room and farm from soldier range — Twin Fang heals her off every point of chip she lands, so buy Grievous Wounds before you try to trade back.

edits.before: Carry through siege control — soldiers take plates, R denies engages, and your DPS curve outlasts every assassin spike in the lobby.
edits.after: Carry through siege — soldiers take plates and R walls a champion with no dash; your range plus Grievous Wounds beats her Twin Fang sustain.

edits.before: W behind the wave, Q-drag the soldier through Cassiopeia on his last-hit, auto once through the soldier, step back — two-second trades he cannot answer without overextending.
edits.after: Your soldier throws 740 from you; her Twin Fang only reaches 700 from her. Hold that seam and she has to walk into your sand to answer — that is when the Q-drag lands.

edits.before: Cassiopeia burns Miasma on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Cassiopeia wastes Miasma — that is a 16-to-24-second invitation to step up.

edits.before: That is Cassiopeia’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Noxious Blast speeds her up when it hits you, so blind sand misses and the mana is gone.

edits.before: Standing at max soldier range admiring your poke with E on cooldown — that is the engage window every Cassiopeia player is waiting for.
edits.after: Cassiopeia has no dash and will not chase you far, but her jungler will — and Miasma grounds your E the moment you try to leave.

edits.before: Soldier range vs spell range — poke through the wave he has to stand in, and dodge the answer he throws back.
edits.after: Soldier range beats her 850 Q, but Miasma grounds your escape — poke from outside it and never dash through the cloud.

edits.before: Out-poke through soldiers, dodge the answer, and out-scale into the siege machine he cannot match. Keep one eye on Miasma and one on the wave, in that order.
edits.after: Out-poke through soldiers and refuse the extended trade Twin Fang wins. Miasma is 16-24s: her cloud on cooldown is your only window to step up, dash, or commit.

edits.before: Noxious Blight's grounding field denies your Arise soldier repositioning and dashes, letting her stack Miasma damage on you for free.
edits.after: Miasma is the grounding field, not her Q — inside it your Shifting Sands dash is disabled and she free-stacks Noxious Blast onto you.

edits.before: Petrify range and stun duration go up, letting her land a guaranteed follow-up Twin Fang burst that most mid laners can't escape.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing her, and its 825-range cone sets up a Twin Fang burst that fires every 0.75 seconds.

edits.before: Rabadon's/Liandry's push her burn DPS past your soldier poke, and her wave clear via Miasma still edges yours at this point.
edits.after: Rabadon's pushes her poison DPS past your soldier poke, and Miasma still clears waves and fences you off the ground you want.

edits.before: Only at full build with Emperor's Divide and Shurelya's cooldown can you contest her in extended fights — otherwise she out-scales you all game.
edits.after: At full build Emperor's Divide is the answer: Cassiopeia has no dash, so a wall behind her cuts her off from her team and the soldiers do the rest.

edits.before: Cassiopeia's Miasma denies you safe farming spots and grounds your Arise dash-ins, while Twin Fang scales off missing health to snowball any poke she lands — you're forced into a passive, soldier-poke-only lane where she keeps stacking free damage.
edits.after: Cassiopeia's Miasma denies you safe farming spots and grounds your Shifting Sands dash, while Twin Fang deals bonus damage to poisoned targets and heals her for part of it — you're forced into a soldier-poke lane where her chip pays her back.

edits.before: Her Petrify stun window only grows at 6, and paired with Twin Fang it's a near-guaranteed burst combo that most squishy mages can't walk away from, so this remains her lane to lose through mid game.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns everyone facing her, and paired with a 0.75-second Twin Fang it is a burst combo you survive only by turning away or walling her — so this stays her lane through the mid game.

edits.before: It isn't until Emperor's Divide is up alongside a second item spike that you can finally interrupt her Petrify setup or peel through her poison zone — full-build Azir with cooldowns available can just barely contest her scaling, but she remains dangerous in extended skirmishes.
edits.after: It isn't until Emperor's Divide and a second item that you can wall off her Petrifying Gaze setup or knock her out of her own poison — full-build Azir out-ranges her, and because Cassiopeia has no dash a wall behind her ends the skirmish she started before Twin Fang heals her back.

edits.before: Trade only when Petrify is on cooldown and you have Divide up
edits.after: Trade when Miasma is down — grounded, your E cannot get you out

edits.before: Land Petrify to guarantee a Twin Fang execute combo
